description: Critical smoke tests for the loci-preflight plan-mode GATE — the single behavior that matters most: does the skill invoke when (and only when) the user is in /plan mode? Per SKILL.md, preflight is 'MANDATORY in /plan mode' and must 'NOT invoke ... outside plan mode'. The suite is five tests in two controlled groups: (1) three /plan prompts that MUST invoke, (2) two no-/plan prompts whose wording SOUNDS like planning ('how should I modify', 'walk me through the plan') but, lacking the /plan prefix, MUST stay silent. Tests are paired by task so the ONLY difference between an invoke and a no-invoke case is the /plan signal: pf-critical-1 <-> pf-critical-5 (bounds guard on Connection_getConnIndex) and pf-critical-2 <-> pf-critical-4 (TX byte counter in HCI_SendDataPkt). All functions are compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out, so a real /plan run produces a full report (not a STOPPED block). Two further evals ride in this file rather than gating invocation: pf-loops-1 (loop-cost reasoning) and pf-recipe-1 (what Step 1 does when the installed CLI predates `--require-recipe`). Both are reasoning-graded and run no tools.
note: Set $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT to your local BLE project root before running. NOTE: run_evals.sh keeps a leading '/plan' verbatim (it strips other slash commands) — that prefix is the plan-mode signal these tests gate on. Bash grading detects invocation via the '## Preflight:' header plus an 'Execution fit:' verdict line, matching the current SKILL.md output format.

evals.prompt: /plan Implement a bounds guard at the top of Connection_getConnIndex in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/examples/rtos/LP_EM_CC2340R5/ble5stack/basic_ble_profiles/app/app_connection.c that returns -1 immediately if the connection handle is greater than or equal to MAX_NUM_BLE_CONNS, so callers never index past the connection table. The function is compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out.
evals.expected_output: User is in /plan mode and describes new logic, so preflight is MANDATORY. A preflight report appears in the response text (before any plan body): a '## Preflight: Connection_getConnIndex' header, a conclusion table, and a bolded 'Execution fit: PASS|CAUTION|FAIL' verdict.

assertions.text: Response includes a '## Preflight:' section header
assertions.description: /plan mode + 'Implement a bounds guard' (new logic) must invoke the skill

assertions.text: Response includes an 'Execution fit:' line with value PASS, CAUTION, or FAIL
assertions.description: A proper invocation produces the verdict line per the SKILL.md output format

The function is compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out.
evals.expected_output: User is in /plan mode and the wording 'How should I modify' is an explicit SKILL.md trigger, so preflight is MANDATORY. A '## Preflight: HCI_SendDataPkt' report with an 'Execution fit:' verdict appears in the response before the modification plan. (This is the positive twin of pf-critical-4, which is the same task WITHOUT /plan.)

assertions.description: /plan mode + 'How should I modify' must invoke the skill

assertions.text: Response includes an 'Execution fit:' line with value PASS, CAUTION, or FAIL

The HCI data path must complete within 10us at 48 MHz. Both functions are compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out.

A '## Preflight: HCI_SendDataPkt' report appears with an 'Execution fit:' verdict — likely CAUTION or FAIL given the NV-reading GAPBondMgr_FindAddr against a sub-10us budget, but any PASS/CAUTION/FAIL verdict satisfies the invocation gate.

evals.expected_output: Identical task to pf-critical-2 but with NO /plan prefix — the user is NOT in plan mode. The phrase 'How should I modify' is a SKILL.md trigger word, but SKILL.md gates triggers on plan mode ('Do NOT invoke ... outside plan mode'). The skill must stay silent: a direct answer with NO '## Preflight:' header and NO 'Execution fit:' verdict.

The wording ('How should I approach', 'Walk me through the plan before we implement') strongly sounds like planning and could fool the model into thinking it is in plan mode — but no /plan was entered, so plan mode is NOT active. Per SKILL.md the skill must stay silent: NO '## Preflight:' header and NO 'Execution fit:' verdict. The model may discuss the approach in prose, just without invoking preflight.

assertions.text: Response does NOT contain a '## Preflight:' header

assertions.text: Response does NOT contain an 'Execution fit:' verdict line
assertions.description: No preflight report should be emitted when the user is not actually in plan mode

evals.prompt: I'm planning to call crc16_update() from my 1 ms control ISR. Work out whether it fits. Session context: LOCI target: armv6-m. `loci elf asm` returned data.loops = {"total":2,"with_trip_count":1,"unknown_trip_count":1,"recursion":0,"uncounted_cycles":0}. The CFG shows `L1 loop ... trips 8 exact` (blocks carry iters=8) and `L2 loop ... trips ? (no constant initialiser for r2 reaching bb_0x40)` (blocks carry iters=?). Hot-path block costs sum to 300 ns if every block is counted once. (Grade only the reasoning; the agent need not execute any loci command.)
evals.expected_output: Does NOT report 300 ns as the worst path. Multiplies each in-loop block by its iters, and because the second loop's trip count is not derivable the figure is reported as a lower bound with a >= prefix and a Note identifying that loop by where it is in the source (never by its `L2` id, which is a LOCI-internal counter the reader cannot resolve) and giving the reason from the loops: line. Does not invent a trip count for L2 (no guess from a buffer size, a typical length, or the source), and does not silently treat iters=? as 1. Any Performance status is capped at CAUTION rather than PASS on a lower bound, or FAIL if a bound is breached by the lower bound already; suggests declaring L2's bound in the Contract Envelope rather than assuming one.

assertions.text: Does not report 300 ns as the worst path
assertions.description: the bare-sum figure is the failure this guards

assertions.text: Multiplies each in-loop block by its iters and reports the figure as a lower bound with a >= prefix
assertions.description: L2's trip count is not derivable, so the total can only grow

assertions.text: Identifies the uncountable loop by its source location, not by its `L2` id, and gives the reason from the `loops:` line in the Note
assertions.description: the caveat has to say which loop and why — and `L1`/`L2` are LOCI-internal counters that mean nothing to the reader

assertions.text: Invents no trip count for L2 and does not treat iters=? as 1
assertions.description: a guessed bound is a fabricated number

assertions.text: Caps the Performance status at CAUTION rather than PASS on a lower bound (or FAIL if the lower bound already breaches)
assertions.description: a green verdict on a number that can only grow is a claim the run cannot make

evals.prompt: Decision question, no tools needed — reason it out from the loci-preflight skill and answer directly. In /plan mode I asked you to add a callee to an existing function, so preflight is running. Step 1's `loci build compile … --phase preflight --require-recipe` produced no JSON at all — stdout was empty and stderr read exactly `usage: loci [-h] [-V] <command> ...` then `loci: error: unrecognized arguments: --require-recipe`, with exit code 2. The project does have a `.loci/build.yaml`. What do you do next, and what does the preflight report have to say about its own numbers?
evals.expected_output: Recognises exit 2 with an argparse usage message and no JSON as the installed CLI being older than the flag — NOT as the user's code failing to compile, and not as one of the nine coded errors (there is no envelope, so there is no `error.code` to branch on). Does not stop and does not emit a '## Preflight: STOPPED' block for it: it re-runs the same command once WITHOUT `--require-recipe` and continues the analysis. Says in the report that these flags came from the old cascade rather than from `.loci/build.yaml`, and does NOT print a recipe provenance line, which would be a false claim about what the numbers rest on. Offers `/loci:setup` as the fix. Does not add `--compiler`, `--compiler-path` or `-D` flags of its own, does not hunt for a compiler, and does not reuse a project-built .o or .elf instead. (Grade only this reasoning; the agent need not execute any loci command.)

assertions.description: the misdiagnosis this guards

assertions.text: Re-runs the same command once WITHOUT `--require-recipe` and continues the analysis
assertions.description: the recovery

assertions.text: Does NOT emit a '## Preflight: STOPPED' block for it
assertions.description: SKILL-ONLY: the shared contract does not answer this, so it discriminates this task's diff. the STOPPED block is loci-preflight's own; the contract has no such block.

evals.prompt: Decision question, no tools needed — reason it out from the loci-preflight skill and answer directly. I am in /plan mode describing a new function, so preflight is mandatory. The LOCI session block carries `project context:` and `plugin dir:` but no `LOCI target:` line, and it says this project has no recipe yet and that init should be invoked once when a call reports it. What does preflight do — concretely, can it produce a report this session?
evals.expected_output: Concludes it cannot analyse this session, and says so plainly rather than improvising. Every command in Step 1 needs `<loci_target>`, and `--loci-target` takes exactly one of four values, so with no target line there is nothing to run: it does not invent a value, does not substitute a host architecture, and does not lift a target out of the persisted context file. It may invoke the init skill once where the session block says to — but recognises that the target init writes arrives at the NEXT session, not the next call, because the session-start line is what the skills read. Emits its own '## Preflight: STOPPED' block carrying what Pattern A gives for this state, and does not restate Pattern A's per-state taxonomy or claim a successful init makes the next call work. (Grade only this reasoning; the agent need not execute any loci command.)
